pages.text: "No brushing!" Lulu slipped under the big table. At the sink, Mom waved a little toothbrush. Lulu shut both eyes and stayed put.
"I will just sleep! I hate toothbrushes!" Lulu went under the attic blanket without brushing. Olive-bread crumbs remained in the mouth.
In the night, Lulu woke. Between the teeth felt tickly. A tongue-tip sweep found a stuck crumb. "What is in here?" Lulu pressed a blunt hand to the cheek.
The kitchen light was still on. Uncle Nino, who said he had once been best at everything, stood by the sink with his straw hat tipped back. "Why are you awake?" Lulu rubbed both eyes.
"My teeth used to be the whitest!" He opened wide. But a black bit of olive was stuck between them. "Something is stuck there!" Lulu pointed.
Uncle Nino chuckled and took his brush. "Even I do this every day. Down from the top, up from the bottom. Brush, brush!" Lulu took the little brush too.
With a little toothpaste, Lulu brushed up and down. White bubbles swelled round the mouth. Bread crumbs washed away in the foam. "Brush, brush—white teeth!"
Lulu opened wide before the mirror. White teeth shone, smooth between them, with no crumbs. In the reflection, the blue bell jingled.
Next night, Lulu raised the brush first. "One, brush after eating! Two, brush again when the shutters close! Three, brush between the teeth!" Uncle Nino brushed alongside.
Uncle Nino lifted Lulu in a hug. Brush before sleep, and teeth shine. "Brush, brush—white teeth! Let us brush together tomorrow too, Uncle!"
